rulings.evidence: REFUSED the board's near-miss baby-back-ribs: that is a PORK loin rib, a different species and a different price class, and it is the same class of error as mapping tteok onto rice-cakes. Boneless beef short ribs is a different primal with no bone in its grams. No beef rib id exists in any namespace, so a new id is proposed.

'Cayenne' unqualified in a spice rub is cayenne pepper; cayenne-pepper is a live id at 6 of 7 stores with an existing label row. Not a new food - the new-food-suspect flag is only because the bare word shares no token with the vocabulary name.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Checked by food, not by string, across all four namespaces: commodities.json carries baby-back-ribs (label 'Baby Back Ribs' - PORK loin rib, wrong species and a different price class), recipe-commodities.json carries no rib id, and the everyday board's only beef rib item is 'Boneless Short Beef Ribs (About 4 per Pack)' under boneless-beef-short-ribs, which is the CHUCK cut, boneless, and sold at a premium per pound. Beef back ribs are the bone-in rack left after the ribeye is lifted, sell as a cheap bone-in rack, and carry roughly half their weight as bone - so the grams basis differs as sharply as the price. Word-order and synonym variants searched: back ribs, beef ribs, rib rack. Nothing prices this food today.

registrar_rulings.reason: No id prices this food: baby-back-ribs is the pork loin rack, beef-short-ribs (live at Baker's) and boneless-beef-short-ribs (board, chuck, boneless premium) are the short-rib cut, and the feed/alias-map/allowlist/vocab hold nothing for the bone-in beef rack, so beef-back-ribs is a genuine new id — but mint it with THREE guards or it collides on day one: (1) baby-back-ribs' include pattern \bback\s+ribs\b will claim 'Beef Back Ribs' product names, so add \bbeef\b to baby-back-ribs' excludes and anchor the new include on beef\s+back\s+ribs; (2) record allowlist pairs vs baby-back-ribs (different species) and beef-short-ribs/boneless-beef-short-ribs (different cut/form) so the dupe audit never re-flags them; (3) it also needs a NEW vocabulary row 'Beef Back Ribs' (vocab returned UNKNOWN, and the boneless-short-rib neighbor is a different form/grams basis) — the name and the id are separate mints. Namespace: recipe-only (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities.json), unit lb, with excludes at neighboring-commodity rigor (sauce/seasoned/fully-cooked/pork at minimum, ~150-pattern class).

macro_cross_check.verdict: CALORIES PASS, PROTEIN FLAGGED. Calories land within 7.4% and carbohydrate within 16% on the low side, which says the portion itself is right. The 28% protein shortfall is NOT a portion error and I am confident of that: 57 g/serving x 4 needs 228 g of protein, which would take about 1.2 kg of pure edible meat - roughly 70% of a 4 lb rack - and beef back ribs are the boniest common rib cut. The source appears to have costed the bone as meat. I took the TOP of the stated 3-4 lb range specifically to close as much of that gap as the recipe honestly allows. Recipe still passes both run conditions (563 cal, 27 g carb). Caveat stated plainly: the ribs macro row rests on two disclosed estimates, a 45% edible yield and a lean-only basis chosen because the recipe directs draining the rendered fat, and both are flagged needs_verify.
